title: Sample 17-7: Word List with Two Different Print Symbols

illustrates.quote: When items in a list are marked with a special shape or icon, follow print for the symbol used. If a print symbol does not have a corresponding symbol in braille, devise a symbol using a shape indicator or a transcriber-defined symbol indicator. a. Begin the symbol or icon in cell 1 followed by at least one space. d. List all symbols/icons on the Special Symbols page, or in a transcriber's note before the text.

blocks.text: Watch out for frequently misspelled words!
blocks.features: prefixed by a pencil icon (devised braille symbol, F-213 — no print character to build from)
prefixed by a pointing-finger icon (devised braille symbol, F-213); the given braille's own embedded TN explains the finger icon means 'this is a bonus word'

print.notes: Two key lines (each introduced by a devised icon — a pencil, a pointing finger — with no print character), then a boxed two-column list (print's own column layout collapsed to one column per 17.5.1c) in which two items ('Illinois', 'our', 'outside') carry the same devised icon markers inline.
print.printFeatures: Two icon-prefixed key lines; a two-column boxed word list with two items individually icon-marked.

braille.notes: Byte-identical between A and B; matches independent re-extraction exactly.

resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Braille unchanged. illustrates.rule: A's '17.5.1' kept over B's wrong '17.4' (a different rule, about partial-emphasis word lists, not marked/icon lists) — the source's own cross-reference at the end of clause d explicitly names 'Sample 17-7'. Modeled with the icon markers dropped (no print character exists for a genuine picture icon — recorded via `features`, not guessed as some placeholder glyph, matching F-213's own finding that an unmapped icon leaks a raw hex escape rather than any braille sign); the box's own multi-column layout is collapsed to one column, matching 17.5.1c's own requirement AND Emboss's own only-ever-one-column list behaviour (F-34, cited here as confirming, not a gap, per standards-map.md's own BANA 17.5.1c row).
